item.research_question: How does the addition of Ni to the immiscible equiatomic CoCrCu system affect liquid state miscibility and solidification behavior, and can in-situ neutron imaging capture this remixing process?
item.material_system: Equiatomic CoCrCu buttons with added elemental Ni buttons to form equiatomic CoCrCuNi (CoCrCu + Ni)
item.processing_route: Arc-melted CoCrCu buttons and remelted Ni buttons placed in an alumina crucible inside a high-temperature vacuum furnace (HOT-A furnace) at ≈1 × 10−6 mbar; heated to 1500 °C, held for 150 radiographs (approx. 35 min), then cooled to 1000 °C
item.test_conditions: In-situ neutron imaging at CG-1D Neutron Imaging Instrument using cold neutrons (0.8 < λ < 6 Å); 10 radiographs acquired every 20 °C from 1000 °C to 1500 °C and back to 1000 °C; ramp rate 20 °C/min; acquisition time 10 s/radiograph; spatial resolution ~200 μm
key_findings: Onset of melting observed at approximately 1100 °C, with complete dissolution of phases at ~1420 °C.
Solidification of the CoCrCuNi alloy initiates at ~1320 °C.
No changes in neutron attenuation were observed during the solidification of the CoCrCuNi alloy, indicating solidification from a single-phase liquid.
Thermodynamic calculations indicate the CoCrCuNix alloy solidifies from a single-phase liquid when x ≥ 0.275, close to the nominal concentration of x = 0.25.
The CT images of the solidified CoCrCuNi alloy show uniform contrast with no macroscopic-phase separations, unlike the heterogeneous CoCrCu alloy.
The miscibility gap in the CoCrCu system is eliminated by the addition of Ni, allowing the Cu-rich liquid to enter the solution.
The furnace thermocouple temperature is estimated to be about 15 °C higher than the sample during heating.
item.mechanism: Ni acts as a solubility pathway for the Cu-rich liquid phase to enter the solution with the overall melt, transforming the previously immiscible CoCr-rich and Cu-rich liquids into a single-phase liquid upon dissolution.
item.limitations: The accuracy of the temperature measurements is within ±15 °C due to the difference between furnace thermocouple readings and actual sample temperature.
item.future_work: The authors propose that in-situ neutron imaging of solidification can provide a novel solution to probe the liquid phases of calculated isopleths and provide valuable insight into the liquid state behavior of HEAs.
quotes: The neutron imaging shows that the solidification of CoCrCuNi results from a single-phase liquid.
The added Ni in this system acts as a solubility pathway for Cu to enter the solution with the rest of the alloying elements.
This novel imaging process showed the phase-separated liquids remixing into a single-phase liquid when Ni dissolves into the melt.
